newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Ord Minnett NZ growth indicator rebounds in August.
newsitem.headline: Ord Minnett NZ growth indicator rebounds in August.

text.p: Ord Minnett's New Zealand growth indicator rebounded a little in August as the stimulatory impact of the July 1 tax cuts started to offset the negative effect of monetary policy, Ord Minnett said on Friday.
The indicator rose to 105.2 in August, up from 104.0 in July, but down from 108.1 in August 1995.

Ord Minnett economist Rodney Dickens said early evidence suggested the combined impact of tight monetary policy and a stimulatory fiscal policy would not result in economic growth being high enough to generate inflation problems next year.
"If our interpretation of the leading indicators is correct, then scope exists for a moderate easing in monetary conditions over the next several months," Dickens said.
The future outlook varied considerably for industries sensitive to high interest rates, relative to those which were benefiting directly from the tax cuts.

"Some industries still have not felt the full negative impact from the rise in interest rates earlier this year, such as residential construction, car imports, spending on plant and equipment and possibly non-residential construction," Dickens said.
The first round of the government's two-year, NZ$3.1 billion income tax and social spending package was implemented on July 1. The next round of tax cuts is scheduled for mid 1997.
